answer: Reputation thread inheritance tax: each new identity starts with a credit score inherited from the thread of identities that funded its creation, and that inherited score decays along a river of prior links. Concretely, an attacker pays a rising marginal fee per identity equal to the summed exposure of every ancestor in its funding terrace, so N identities cost roughly N² in locked collateral released only after sustained honest activity. Cost shifts from a fixed gate to a steep curve.
